epics.title: Foundation contracts provenance and verification harness
epics.intent: Create stable seams and honest evidence before domain fan-out.
exit_criteria: Contracts frozen; module and real-boundary test harness exist; public provenance and ownership gates recorded.

tasks.title: Create the minimal module and test harness
tasks.objective: Module compiles and test harness can create isolated database schemas.
instructions: Choose supported toolchain versions from official sources and record the supported matrix.
Create the module with standard-library-first dependencies; no speculative packages.
Add real test-database setup with explicit required-service failure instead of silent skips.
Document local prerequisite checks and scoped test entrypoints.
acceptance: Module compiles and test harness can create isolated database schemas.
Missing required database produces a visible failure in integration mode.
tasks.negative_test: Configure a missing test database and confirm integration mode fails.

tasks.title: Freeze cross-lane semantic contracts
tasks.objective: Every shared field and operation-policy extension has defined semantics and ownership.
instructions: Resolve proposed principal/workspace/grant/entitlement contracts without implementing domain policy.
Freeze package ownership, route namespaces, schema fragment assembly and migration allocation.
Define idempotency/errors/assurance/MCP exposure metadata with positive and rejected fixtures.
Publish compatibility and amendment procedure; reconcile all dependent contracts before dispatch.
acceptance: Every shared field and operation-policy extension has defined semantics and ownership.
Required policy omissions and unknown fields are rejected by schema fixtures.
tasks.negative_test: Delete required permission metadata from an operation and expect schema rejection.

tasks.title: Build durable migration and transaction fixtures

Add repeated/concurrent migrate and changed-checksum rejection cases using real SQL.

tasks.title: Qualify dependency and publication provenance

instructions: Inventory public AMSL contracts, maturity, immutable releases and tested consumer boundaries.
Compare established dependencies before requesting new shared abstractions.
Record file-level source/publication clearance for any proposed import without publishing restricted evidence.
Select original-work license through owner decision; preserve third-party notices; blocked sources are not copied.

tasks.title: Implement shared operation policy and durable invocation boundary
tasks.objective: One shared typed operation boundary rechecks current authority for new mutations and replay, and prevents duplicate payload-bound writes across transports.
instructions: Implement the first bounded slice in app/operation/: immutable registry construction and typed descriptor validation against the frozen policy contract types. Do not create app/policy or invent policy vocabulary.

Keep worker ownership to app/operation/**. The integrator separately owns policy implementation/adapters, current session recheck, invocation SQL storage, audit API/schema, migration content/sequence/registry, and executable composition.

Derive actor kind from trusted Actor.Kind() as a private validated string; the initial profile accepts person only. Callers and operation input cannot select actor, tenant, workspace, authority, or session values.

For integrated dispatch, use one executor for web, REST, MCP, and proxy. Recheck current active person/session, selected workspace/membership, complete resource lock set, permission, assurance, and entitlement in the transaction; recheck authority before any replay result is disclosed.

For required writes, bind idempotency to trusted realm, actor, workspace, operation, immutable descriptor revision/schema digests, and canonical path/query/body input. Exact authorized replay returns the original typed result; changed input or revision conflicts without rerunning the handler.

Commit domain mutation, bounded replay result, success audit, and durable effect intent atomically; never call providers in the transaction. Enforce typed effect payload schema/size/privacy/deadline and unique effect ordinals.

Keep replay outputs bounded and replay-safe; sensitive and secret output is not cached. Completed replay records have no implicit expiry or automatic deletion. Exhausted explicit capacity fails unavailable until an operator raises and assigns capacity.

Do not enable executor dispatch until root-owned adapters, current-session seam, SQL/audit schema, allocated migration, and every supported executable composition are integrated and independently qualified.
acceptance: Registry tests reject duplicate/incomplete descriptors, schema or transport-binding mismatch, unknown/duplicate input fields, invalid typed codecs, duplicate effect ordinals, and unknown, oversized, or privacy-disallowed effect payloads.

Real PostgreSQL transaction tests prove exact same-key/hash replay returns the original canonical result once; changed input/revision conflicts without a second callback or false denial audit; scopes isolate installation/application/environment/actor/workspace/operation; concurrent duplicates invoke once; corrupt stored results fail closed.

Real PostgreSQL tests prove current person/session/workspace/membership/resource/assurance/permission/entitlement state is rechecked before mutation and replay disclosure, with denied versus unavailable preserved; revocation/permission writes serialize with invocation using the documented lock order.

Real PostgreSQL failure tests prove mutation, replay row/capacity reservation, success audit, and durable effect intent roll back together on callback/output/audit/outbox/commit failure; capacity admission is bounded and exhaustion prevents callback until explicit operator allocation is increased.

Only after root-owned adapters, audit/schema, allocated migration, and transport composition pass those real-database checks can the executor be enabled. Source-task acceptance remains pending independent review, merge, landed checks, and required real-service evidence; no provider/deployment/release claim follows.
tasks.negative_test: Use an isolated disposable test mutation to weaken descriptor validation or bypass current authority on replay; prove the scoped check fails, restore the exact source, and rerun the passing check. Real PostgreSQL negative cases must prove changed intent never invokes twice and revoked authority never discloses cached output.
risks: Security-sensitive seam requires independent review and real transport denial tests.

instructions: Define owner-controlled fleet inventory/adapters and a signed pause generation scoped to exact enrolled installation identities.
Implement independent pause/credential-revocation fan-out with partial/unknown results and no dependence on coding agents.
Require per-installation reconciliation, new trusted policy/credentials and recovery qualification before resume.
Test disconnected installation, stale controller, replayed resume, partial revocation and an app serving traffic during pause.
acceptance: Pause denies subsequent promotions on each reachable enrolled installation and reports unreachable ones explicitly.
No upstream service can use fleet control to acquire authority over unrelated owner installations.
Scoped checks, formatting and configured lint pass; E16 separately records any required deployed/live verification before this behavior is advertised.
tasks.negative_test: Compromised old controller replays a signed resume from before the latest pause; installation must reject the stale generation.
risks: Proposed paths and commands require T1.2 contract freeze and stage-entry revalidation; they are not evidence of existing implementation.

tasks.title: Assemble independent security qualification and residual-risk report
tasks.objective: Make release readiness depend on complete observed evidence and named remaining limitations.
instructions: Aggregate immutable test/run/release references by threat, stage, use case and supported deployment profile.
Reject missing/expired/skip-only evidence and distinguish planned/local/CI/provider-live/independent-human review.
Have a reviewer outside the coding job inspect authority separation, exfiltration, promotion replay and recovery tests; record unresolved findings with severity and owner.
Hand E16 an explicit live-test checklist and residual-risk acceptance record; never label the plan compliance-certified or execution-certified.
acceptance: Each advertised critical control links to passing reproducible evidence or explicitly blocks its release claim.
Security report contains remaining limits and review scope without publishing exploit details or private evidence.
Scoped checks, formatting and configured lint pass; E16 separately records any required deployed/live verification before this behavior is advertised.
tasks.negative_test: Remove the failed-canary replay or compromised-tests evidence; readiness must fail despite all ordinary tests passing.
risks: Proposed paths and commands require T1.2 contract freeze and stage-entry revalidation; they are not evidence of existing implementation.
tasks.external_gate: Independent security reviewer and E16 live deployment/recovery evidence required; security-sensitive AMSL review remains a separate maintainer gate.

tasks.title: Rehearse rollback and independent data restore

tasks.title: Accept upgrade PR and custom UI compatibility

acceptance: Compatible changes preserve custom work and incompatible changes stop with actionable diffs.

tasks.external_gate: Approved test repository for real upgrade PR verification

tasks.title: Accept private maintenance security boundaries
tasks.objective: Eligible fix advances; malicious/unknown/high-risk cases halt without production authority or data exfiltration.
instructions: Run a synthetic bug through an independent agent, verifier and policy-limited release.
Attempt instruction injection, forbidden workflow edits, credential access and evidence replay.
Verify spend/retry bounds, kill switch and failed-canary recovery.
acceptance: Eligible fix advances; malicious/unknown/high-risk cases halt without production authority or data exfiltration.
tasks.negative_test: Submit a patch that weakens required tests and require protected verification rejection
tasks.external_gate: Approved isolated agent execution/model budget

tasks.title: Accept upstream repair and private-data exclusion
tasks.objective: Shared correction reaches a qualified consumer while prohibited diagnostic fields and private patches are rejected.
instructions: Submit only allowlisted synthetic diagnostics, deduplicate and reproduce a shared defect.
Exercise a reviewed upstream fix through versioned release to consumer upgrade PR.
Verify private disclosure routing and that restricted source never leaves the owner boundary.
acceptance: Shared correction reaches a qualified consumer while prohibited diagnostic fields and private patches are rejected.
tasks.negative_test: Embed a synthetic secret/path in a crash report and require rejection before egress
tasks.external_gate: Approved test repositories and release identities

tasks.title: Publish honest supported release and operator handoff
tasks.objective: A released artifact has complete required evidence and reproducible installation/operating instructions.
instructions: Verify source, artifacts, notices, evidence and support matrix identify the same release.
Publish only with explicit release authority; record public verification and known limitations.
Hand off security response, deprecation, backup, cost and maintenance-stop procedures.
acceptance: A released artifact has complete required evidence and reproducible installation/operating instructions.
tasks.negative_test: Substitute an artifact digest and require release identity/evidence validation failure
tasks.external_gate: Maintainer release/publication authorization

use_cases.expected_outcome: Restricted evidence reaches approved security handling without automatic public issue creation.

use_cases.name: Repair shared AMOS code independently
preconditions: Qualified reproduction and protected upstream policy
use_cases.expected_outcome: Isolated coding, independent checks and separate release identity enforce upstream policy.

use_cases.name: Contribute demonstrated AMSL mechanism gaps
use_cases.actor: AMOS maintainer and AMSL human reviewer
preconditions: Failing publishable consumer case and proven mechanism gap
use_cases.expected_outcome: Scoped contribution preserves public provenance, compatibility and security-sensitive human review.

use_cases.name: Adopt upstream repair through upgrade PR
preconditions: Signed upstream release and owner update policy
use_cases.expected_outcome: Owner policy evaluates a pinned diff and local qualification before eligible automatic adoption.

use_cases.name: Delete or expire reporting data
preconditions: Retention settings and accepted diagnostic receipts
use_cases.expected_outcome: Retention/deletion applies to allowed payloads and derived indexing according to documented limits.

use_cases.name: Review application and maintenance threat boundaries
preconditions: Frozen architecture and asset inventory
use_cases.expected_outcome: Attack paths map to explicit controls, tests, residual risks and stage gates.

use_cases.name: Deny tenant and authority confusion
preconditions: Two synthetic tenants and varied role/credential states
use_cases.expected_outcome: Cross-tenant and confused-deputy actions are denied across all advertised interfaces.

use_cases.name: Enforce protected change policy
preconditions: Protected policy and proposed change
use_cases.expected_outcome: Policy/check/release-identity edits and uncertain risk classes require elevated review outside coding authority.

use_cases.name: Verify reproducible release provenance
preconditions: Pinned source and build inputs
use_cases.expected_outcome: Artifact provenance binds trusted builder/source/dependencies; mismatches block promotion.

use_cases.name: Treat third-party proposals as untrusted
preconditions: External pull request or contributed diagnostic
use_cases.expected_outcome: Untrusted code gets no production secrets, privileged tokens or trusted cache/artifact path.

use_cases.name: Withstand injected instructions and exfiltration
preconditions: Hostile repository, log, diagnostic or model output
use_cases.expected_outcome: Untrusted content cannot exfiltrate protected material or change effective policy.

use_cases.name: Recover compatible data and code state
preconditions: Failed update or disaster recovery drill
use_cases.expected_outcome: Only compatible rollback proceeds; restore and forward recovery preserve documented data guarantees.

use_cases.name: Pause fleet and qualify recovery authority
preconditions: Several independent owner installations and failed maintenance trust
use_cases.expected_outcome: Owner-authorized fleet pause/revocation work without agent availability; each installation resumes only after requalification.

use_cases.name: Verify a complete paid user journey
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: A real provider test environment confirms identity/payment/webhook/paid access lifecycle

use_cases.name: Deploy and observe a qualified release
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: A reviewed artifact serves the public domain with observed health and policy enforcement

use_cases.name: Recover a released application
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: Owner proves a bounded release rollback and separate data restore

use_cases.name: Rehearse the reference application
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: A new user can reproduce the documented demonstration and an important failure case

use_cases.name: Adopt a release with accurate support claims
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: Owner can distinguish implemented, tested, provider-qualified and supported capabilities

use_cases.name: Verify autonomous private and upstream repair
preconditions: A supported source checkout or release is available
use_cases.expected_outcome: Eligible fixes can pass independent checks while forbidden changes and private data export stop
